title: Thermally melted quadrupolar order and intrinsically quantum phases in 5$d^1$ double perovskites
authors: Rong Cong, Ginevra Corsale, Ilija K. Nikolov, Wenjuan Zhang, Nandini Trivedi, Vesna F. Mitrović
abstract: Spin-orbit-coupled $d^1$ double perovskites exhibit a rich interplay of spin, orbital, and quadrupolar degrees of freedom (DOF), giving rise to competing magnetic and multipolar phases. Although quantum mean-field theories predict many exotic phases, their stability against thermal fluctuations and reproducibility within a classical framework remain an open question. Here, we surpass the mean-field limitations by deploying large-scale classical Monte Carlo simulations on the projected $j=3/2$ manifold of the FCC lattice, allowing complex ordering patterns to emerge spontaneously without preassigned magnetic symmetries. Our thermodynamic mapping reveals that thermal fluctuations melt the intermediate-temperature quadrupolar phase over part of the phase diagram, while it survives intact elsewhere. Crucially, by systematically isolating the boundary between classical and quantum stability, we demonstrate that while the four-sublattice antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic (FM) phases are robustly classical, the coplanar canted FM[110] state completely destabilizes. This identifies the FM[110] phase as an intrinsically quantum state born out of quantum fluctuations. Our results demonstrate that the dominant magnetic phases are robust within a classical description, where the essential physics of the system is captured by weakly entangled, short-range correlated DOF and highlight the role of thermal fluctuations in determining the stability of different types of magnetic and quadrupolar order.
summary: This study uses large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to map the complex phase diagram of $5d^1$ double perovskites, which feature coupled spin, orbital, and quadrupolar degrees of freedom. The research distinguishes between phases stable under classical thermal fluctuations and those that require quantum mechanical treatment. It establishes that the FM[110] state is intrinsically quantum, while the dominant magnetic phases are robustly classical.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex interplay between spin, orbital, and quadrupolar degrees of freedom in $5d^1$ double perovskites and determines the stability of exotic magnetic and multipolar phases against thermal fluctuations.
main_result: The simulations show that while the AFM and FM 4-sublattices are robustly classical, the coplanar canted FM[110] state destabilizes, identifying it as an intrinsically quantum state.
method: The research employs large-scale classical Monte Carlo simulations on the projected $j=3/2$ manifold of the FCC lattice to map the finite-temperature phase diagram.
model_or_system: The system is $5d^1$ double perovskites, modeled with an effective Hamiltonian incorporating nearest-neighbor AFM/FM exchange and electric quadrupole-quadrupole interactions, projected onto the $j=3/2$ basis.
key_observables: Orbital occupations ($\langle	ilde{n}_{\alpha eta}angle$), staggered magnetization ($m_{xy}^{	ext{stg}}$), and various susceptibilities ($\chi^{-1}_{	ext{tot}}$, $\chi^{-1}_{\parallel}$, $\chi^{-1}_{\perp}$).
important_parameters: The ratio of exchange couplings ($J_2/J_1$) and the quadrupolar interaction strength ($V/J_1$) govern the transitions between different ordered phases.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the system's essential physics can be captured by treating the effective moment classically, thereby surpassing mean-field limitations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate orbital occupations and magnetization across different coupling regimes, while correlation functions (FIG. S2-S4) diagnose the nature of order (e.g., long-range FM vs. short-range AFM).
paper_structure: The paper systematically maps the phase diagram by analyzing transitions (PM $	o$ Quad $	o$ FM or PM $	o$ AFM) as a function of coupling constants, using MC simulations to track order parameters and correlation functions.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, fluctuation-driven phase diagram for strongly correlated $5d$ systems, directly addressing the boundary between classical and quantum stability in multiferroic materials.
